title: Who played at the jam sessions at her house
summary: She names Eddie Cole, Panama Francis, Al Morgan, Lloyd Wilson, Forest Powell and Marshall Royal among those at her house sessions.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, she seems to have. When Nat used to rehearse his big band at your house, who was in that big band, do you remember?

I can't remember, frankly. The only person, I think, that I can remember, was his brother Eddie, who was at that time a bass player, and Eddie of course has gone on also. Eddie later got with a group, he had a group, I can't remember what they called themselves, but he had an entertaining group, something like four or five people in it. And I can't -- I can't remember anybody else in the band, I just can't, because when they used to rehearse, well they -- not only would his band be there, some of the other guys would come in and they would start, and before you knew it it was a jam session.
He was such a tremendous pianist, you know, and all the guys just loved to play with him, you know. All of them would.
Who all can you remember from the jam

sessions at your house? Who used to play there? Well, let me see. As I mentioned, Panama Francis was one of the guys. Al Morgan, who's gone on, a marvelous bass player, used to be with Calloway years ago. And Al -- not Al Wilson -- Lloyd Wilson, who was a trumpet player from Detroit, he and his wife shared a house with us, and guys like Forest Powell, a little trumpet player who's also still around, and -- oh, gosh. Well, of course Marshall Royal. Marshall, I've known him and worked with Marshall, I had the pleasure of working with Marshall too.
